chapter_title: Concerning the Dragon with Fourteen Heads; what it is and [...]
chapter_note: The chapter’s core is a systematic microcosmic mapping: the Fourteen Heads are identified with sense/organs (upper and lower), and the Five Dens with specific internal organs/blood—an internal correspondence (body ↔ spiritual ‘Dragon’ mechanism) with no external authorities. The chapter is wrapped in a Q&A frame (disciple ↔ apostle) and closes with a devotional/praise response. A late application/pastoral drift appears where the combat with the Dragon is tied to Manichaean status language (“elect”) and reward rhetoric.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Strong hagiographic/dialogue framing (“Once again… disciple… apostle… I beseech you, my master”). Although it introduces the topic, the paragraph is primarily the compiled Q&A container.

paragraphs.core_text: There is never a Dragon in the flesh with fourteen heads, as the Magi say! Rather, this is a spiritual lesson.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue attribution (“Then the apostle says to him:”). Removed the remaining explanatory continuation about ‘virginity’ and the Magi’s misunderstanding, which shifts from defining the Dragon’s ontological status to polemical/historical commentary external to the correspondence.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Begins with a compilation dialogue tag (late), but preserves a concise ontological correction (corporeal vs. spiritual) consistent with the core’s explanatory voice.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, this is how this earth [ ... ] to it, as it is accounted a corporeal Dragon [ ... ] I will instruct you [ ... ] the Dragon is this doctrine [ ... ] of the flesh [ ... ] also the fourteen heads that are distributed over the Dragon are these.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core-style transition into exposition: defines what the Dragon ‘is’ and announces an enumerative mapping (“the fourteen heads… are these”), with correspondence staying within the anthropological/cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: The seven sense organs on the head of the body are the two of sight by which one sees; the two of sound by which one hears; the two of scent by which one smells; also the tongue [ ... ] by which one selects, receiving there the different tastes that occur in every form.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic, impersonal enumeration (sevenfold schema) mapping faculties/senses—classic substrate correspondential listing.

paragraphs.core_text: These are the seven heads of the Dragon, the seven sense organs that are on the upper part of the person; [ ... ] below. The seven of the torso are these: two [ ... ]; the two [ ... ] ruler [ ... ] the seven heads that are above; so with the ones below they total and make fourteen heads of the Dragon.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Degree-structure arithmetic (7+7=14) extending the mapping from head to torso; the teaching remains internal to the microcosm schema.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.253⟩
Conversely, the five dens about which they have spoken, where the Dragon is congregated and protrudes, are these: the first is the tongue; the second is the lungs; the third is the heart; the fourth is the spleen; the fifth is the blood that dwells in them. Again, if it shall look out from them [and reveal its likeness and its observation above and below, it wages war by] its fourteen heads.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Highly structured fivefold mapping (dens ↔ organs/blood) and mechanistic description (how it ‘looks out’/‘wages war’), characteristic of the older explanatory substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: Whoever will recognise them with the Dragon, which is the thought of the body, and struggles with it and is victorious and kills it in them [ ... he is called]
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the institutional/commendatory titles (“the holy righteous one, elect, good person”) and the reward statement (“He receives the victory without suffering on the day of his coming forth”), which pivot from describing the Dragon-mechanism to applying it to community status and soteriological exhortation.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Starts with a general mechanism-identification (“Dragon… thought of the body”) compatible with the core, then shifts into application voice and Manichaean community terminology (“elect”)—consistent with the chapter’s flagged second-half drift.

paragraphs.core_text: So, behold, I have taught you of the Dragon that exists with its fourteen heads and five dens, wherein it is concealed and hidden. It does through them [ ... / its des]ire all the time.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summative restatement of the defined structure (14 heads, 5 dens) plus a functional claim about continuous operation (“desire all the time”); remains internal to the Dragon/body mechanism without institutional targeting.
Closing disciple response with blessing and eternal-life/victory rhetoric; typical Q&A wrap-up and doxological framing rather than substrate exposition.
